terms.definition: An element in Group 1 — a soft, shiny, extremely reactive metal with one valence electron.
terms.function: Reacts eagerly by losing its single outer electron, becoming a +1 ion.
terms.whereItIs: Group 1 — the first column of the periodic table.
terms.whyItMatters: The alkali metals are the clearest example of how one valence electron creates a family of similar, dramatic behavior.

terms.definition: The single electron in the outermost shell of an alkali metal atom.
terms.function: Is the one electron the atom is eager to give away to reach a full, stable shell.
terms.whereItIs: The lone, highlighted electron on the outer ring in the model.
terms.whyItMatters: One valence electron is the whole reason the alkali metals react so violently.

terms.definition: A +1 positive ion formed when an alkali metal loses its one outer electron.
terms.function: Gives the metal a full stable shell and a positive charge it can use to bond.
terms.whereItIs: Formed in every alkali metal reaction — like sodium becoming Na⁺.
terms.whyItMatters: Sodium and potassium cations are essential to nerve signaling and batteries.

terms.definition: The first column of the periodic table, home to the alkali metals.
terms.function: Stacks the one-electron family together at the far left of the table.
terms.whereItIs: The glowing first column in the model's table section.
terms.whyItMatters: Every element in this column shares the same explosive temperament.
